title: Teaching laboratory 2.14: safety manual, Part 2
genre: lab safety manual with checklist tables

language.typeRulesUnderDefaultLocale: the document declares lang="en"; under the default locale de-DE every run whose language differs from the locale is structurally excluded (docs/rules/type-spaced-hyphen.md 'Limits': 'any run whose lang differs from the locale are structurally excluded, on the ancestor chain')

pages.basis: plain Paged.js measurement: 6 pages with the reference fonts and with DejaVu, 5 with FreeFont (the inspection table and the sign-off sheet shift)

expectedExit.derivation: Under WP-F3 round 2 the split sign-off table (flow hazard table-columns) and the overflow-column row are declined as env/invalid-measurement, which leaves the error rule's coverage below 1 (exit 4) wherever the run is measured. Observed on plain Chromium 141: Paged.js leaves table row #so-42 of #signoff-sheet in the overflow column of its first page (a table box right of the content box, invisible and missing from the PDF). docs/limitations.md: such a table residue makes the PDF diverge from the measured geometry and the run must end in exit 3 render-unstable. A renderer that places the row does not produce the residue; the document then has no required error finding: the two-fragment sheet is the documented gap, which a tool may leave unreported (0) or, having closed the gap, report as an error (1).

byCode.3: render-unstable: table residue observed in the plain probe (expected on the reference renderer)
byCode.1: no residue, two-fragment sheet reported (allowed documented-gap entry)
byCode.4: no residue, sign-off table declined under WP-F3 round 2

expectedExit.environmentNote: Exit 4 with exitReason evidence/required-page-binding-incomplete is an environment failure (evidence binding not supported by the renderer), not an outcome of these documents; run the gate where the live path binds evidence (CI).

fontDependence: Only generic families (serif, sans-serif, monospace) are used. Line breaks, paragraph heights and therefore the position of flowing text depend on the fonts the renderer resolves; every construction fact below is built from explicit heights, fixed line pitches, forced breaks or SVG coordinates so that it does not depend on them, and every font-dependent outcome is listed as allowed.

expectedDeclines.docsBasis: WP-F3 round 2 (G-03/G-81; README 'Release semantics', tracing) replaces the structural sum over three or more fragments with a lower bound from the content extent of each fragment (text lines and replaced content), and declines with env/invalid-measurement, charged to the rule's coverage floor of 1, a split block whose snapshot records a flow hazard (out-of-flow, offset, sticky, transformed, float, multicol, flex-or-grid, table-columns, vertical-writing, negative-margin, overflowing-content), a split block whose bound stays at or below the page (inconclusive), and an unsplit block that is transformed or reaches past the sheet. Not on a rule page when this was written, so required: false.

fontStacks.reference: machine default: Chromium resolves serif, sans-serif, monospace to Liberation Serif, Liberation Sans, DejaVu Sans Mono
fontStacks.free: FONTCONFIG_FILE=probe/fontconfig/free.conf (Liberation and DejaVu rejected: FreeSerif, FreeSans, FreeMono)

notes: Rule-level expectations apply when the document is measured (exit 0/1/4). If the run ends in exit 3 render-unstable, the tool withholds findings by design (docs/limitations.md); the gate then checks the exit reason only.

Independent review (2026-09-24): the first fragment of #signoff-sheet measures 912 px by getBoundingClientRect() but 928.17 px as the CDP layout box, because the row left in the overflow column still belongs to it. A tool that reads the layout box sees a first fragment taller than the 912 px content box; that is one more way to reach exit 1, not a different truth.
